messages:
maria_support: FYI Acme tenant on dedicated eu-west-1 is reporting intermittent 503s from the Redwood API and a concurrent unexpected billing spike this morning. Customer hit us at 07:42 UTC. Can we collect a repro bundle and the relevant request IDs?

kevin_oncall: Oof. Any sample request ids or time ranges? Also which model and pool are they using?

maria_support: They provided this high-level info in the ticket: tenant_id=acme-42, model=redwood-3b-quant, route=/v1/chat/stream, approx timeframe 2026-03-16T07:30:00Z - 2026-03-16T07:50:00Z. No request ids in the ticket, they said retries from the app show 503s and client-side latencies spiking to >10s. Billing spike shows ~x5 token ops within the same window.

jenna_eng_sre: OK let's do standard repro gather but also capture per-request charge metadata and any duplicate retries. Ask them for any client-side request ids (X-Request-Id) or the Authorization-sub-sub header if they pass a custom request id.

maria_support: I asked for X-Request-Id header and one example curl. They pasted this (redacted token):

```bash
curl -v https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/chat/stream \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-3b-quant","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"summarize quarterly"}]}'
```

maria_support: They say the app logs show an internal request id header: req-id=acme-42-20260316-07:38:12-XYZ. I asked for 3 examples, they are collecting.

ashish_ml: From ML/runtime perspective: need the model-server pod logs, the runtime trace (kv cache stats) and any kernel XIDs around that window. Also check if any node-level preemption or GPU OOM happened.

jenna_eng_sre: Right. Maria can you ask customer to run these on their dedicated cluster control plane host (or we can run from our side if they grant us support access). Provide them this ordered checklist:

1) Gather request ids and sample client curl reproducer (we already have the example).
2) Pod logs: `kubectl -n tenants-acme-42 logs deploy/model-server --since=40m --tail=500`
3) Pod env and manifest: `kubectl -n tenants-acme-42 get deploy model-server -o yaml`
4) Node dmesg and journal: `sudo dmesg --ctime | sed -n '1,200p'` and `sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since '2026-03-16 07:20:00' --until '2026-03-16 08:00:00' -o short-precise`
5) GPU state: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,timestamp,utilization.gpu,utilization.memory,temperature.gpu,memory.used --format=csv -l 1 -f /tmp/gpu-sample.csv --loop=30 --count=60` (or `--loop-ms` equivalent on older drivers)
6) System metrics: `curl -s 'http://localhost:9100/metrics' | grep -E 'node_cpu|node_memory|node_disk'` and export prometheus query times for the window (we'll provide queries).
7) Collect model runtime trace: `kubectl -n tenants-acme-42 exec -it deploy/model-server --container runtime -- /bin/bash -c 'cat /var/log/runtime/kvcache.log; ls /tmp/runs'`

maria_support: Sent that checklist and asked for the pod logs + the three req-ids. Also asked if they can run the curl with `-H "X-Request-Id: <id>"` to make it easier to correlate.

kevin_oncall: I'll open a temporary support session token for acme-42 and create upload bucket for the debug bundle. Tagging ops_tooling_bot to generate the bundle script.

ops_tooling_bot: Created S3 pre-signed upload: s3://redwood-debug/acme-42/2640309999-bundle.tar.gz (expires in 24h). Run `redwood-support collect-bundle --tenant acme-42 --since '2026-03-16T07:20:00Z' --until '2026-03-16T08:00:00Z' --upload s3://redwood-debug/acme-42/2640309999-bundle.tar.gz` on a node with rw access.

jenna_eng_sre: If they can't run the tooling, give these manual commands for a minimal bundle:

```bash
mkdir -p /tmp/acme-debug && cd /tmp/acme-debug
kubectl -n tenants-acme-42 get pods -o wide > pods.txt
for p in $(kubectl -n tenants-acme-42 get pods -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do kubectl -n tenants-acme-42 logs $p --all-containers --since=1h > $p.logs 2>&1 || true; done
sudo dmesg -T > dmesg.txt || true
sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since '2026-03-16 07:20:00' --until '2026-03-16 08:00:00' -o short-precise > kubelet-journal.txt || true
nvidia-smi -q -x > nvidia-full.xml || true
tar czf /tmp/acme-42-minimal-debug.tar.gz ./*
# then upload the tarball to the presigned s3 URL
curl -X PUT -T /tmp/acme-42-minimal-debug.tar.gz "<presigned-url>"
```

maria_support: Customer said they can run the minimal steps and will upload. They also asked: could billing spike be caused by automatic client retries? I told them we will check request duplication server-side and token-level counts.

ashish_ml: We should also pull tokenization logs (tokenizer counters) and per-request token charge fields from the accounting DB for tenant acme-42 for that hour. I'll ask infra to run a query.

kevin_oncall: tagging devtools_bot to pull accounting counts. devtools_bot?

devtools_bot: Queued accounting query: SELECT request_id, tenant_id, model, input_tokens, output_tokens, charged_tokens, timestamp FROM billing.requests WHERE tenant_id='acme-42' AND timestamp >= '2026-03-16 07:20:00' AND timestamp <= '2026-03-16 08:00:00'; Results will be posted in this thread when ready.

jenna_eng_sre: Also watch for any autoscaler flapping that could lead to duplicated warmups/duplicate requests. Ask customer to capture `kubectl -n kube-system get hpa,deploy -w` output if autoscaler was active.

maria_support: Upload came in at 08:45 UTC: they put minimal tar at the presigned S3. I'm pulling it now.

jenna_eng_sre: Great — once we have logs I'll look for patterns: identical request_id repeated, 429/503 cascades from the runtime, model-server restarts, or heavy GC on the host. I'll also check kernel XIDs and dmesg for GPU errors.

ashish_ml: If we see frequent KV cache cold misses during a narrow time window and a high duplicate request rate, that can explain both latency and token churn (clients retrying). If KV cache thrash, we may need to adjust per-tenant cache allocation for dedicated pools.

kevin_oncall: Preliminary results from the billing query (small sample): 7 requests show charged_tokens >> input+output (possible double-charging due to retries) — linking logs next.

maria_support: Uploaded bundle is here: s3://redwood-debug/acme-42/2640309999-bundle.tar.gz. Please confirm when you see it.

jenna_eng_sre: Downloading and unpacking now. Will post a short repro summary in ~30m.

ops_tooling_bot: Reminder: please sanitize Authorization header values before posting logs in public channels. Use REDACTED tokens.

maria_support: Noted. I'll scrub client tokens before forwarding.

jenna_eng_sre: Quick findings: model-server hit a burst of concurrent requests at 07:38:10Z, several pods rolled during that minute (kubelet OOM killers on one node). There are repeated entries showing the same req-id being retried 3x from the client side within 30s. Also saw a GPU driver Xid 61 at 07:38:11Z on node gpu-03 (dmesg + nvidia-smi snapshot).

ashish_ml: Xid61 is usually recoverable but can cause a request to fail mid-stream — that would prompt client retries. Billing duplicates could come from retries that were accepted by a fallback model instance that completed the request; the billing pipeline records both. We need to correlate exact request_ids to billing rows and dedupe.

jenna_eng_sre: Action items:
- kevin_oncall: isolate gpu-03 and run `sudo journalctl -k --since '2026-03-16 07:36:00' --until '2026-03-16 07:40:00'` and collect kernel oops, driver backtraces.
- ashish_ml: run dedupe job against billing.requests for those req-ids and mark duplicates for credit if server counted retries twice.
- devtools_bot: add a server-side guard to ensure idempotency for X-Request-Id within a 2m window for dedicated pools (discussion-only for now).

kevin_oncall: I'll spin a maintenance window for gpu-03, cordon + drain if we see repeated GPU XIDs.

maria_support: I'll update the customer: we've identified GPU driver Xid and client retry pattern likely causing both 503s and token duplication. Asking if they want immediate credit or wait until we finish root cause.

ashish_ml: Recommend temporary mitigation: enable server-side idempotency for their tenant or throttle client retries for 30s, and schedule driver update for the node if XIDs persist.

maria_support: Customer asked for ETA. I'll give an initial estimate: 4-6 hours for full RCA and billing remediation plan. Will post updates here.

jenna_eng_sre: Thanks team. Leaving this thread open for follow-ups.
